problem: Two ways to persist a subagent's return; the draft's B5 uses the hook.

questions.text: Who writes a subagent's return to the run folder?
questions.why: The hook needs no agent cooperation and can hold the agent (exit 2) until the return validates; the leaf makes the agent responsible and keeps the hook set smaller. Either way the workflow receives the typed return.

options.value: A global SubagentStop hook: parses, validates, stores, holds the agent on failure (draft B5).
The agent itself, by calling a store leaf as its last act; the hook only checks that the file exists and holds the agent if not.

questions.text: The three manuals still written as runner command sequences (journey, review, workflows): what happens to them in this launch?
questions.why: They are context an agent cannot test. Rewriting is a unit; deleting is cheap and loses nothing a role in this launch reads; leaving them hands every role a false premise.

options.value: Delete them in this launch; the conduct launch writes their successors.
Rewrite them here to artefacts, roles and gates.
Leave them; a header line marks them as describing the superseded runner.
